tasks.title: Dispose the 22 scale-less call sites in DungeonMaster.Tests three ways: 13 mechanical appends, 2 conversions with rename, 7 sites removed with their 5 enclosing [Fact] methods (MASTER-047 / CORE-019, measurement.md section 5)
acceptance: A1. THE 13 MECHANICAL SITES. Each of the 13 call sites enumerated in measurement.md section 5.4 now passes an explicit scale argument, so the call resolves to the scale-carrying overload rather than the scale-less one. The 13, at their b39a65d line numbers (they will move as the files are edited, so locate them by enclosing test method, not by line): RemovePlacedObjectCommandHandlerTests.cs:32 (HandleAsync_ValidCommand_RemovesObjectAndReturnsSuccess); UpdatePlacedObjectCommandHandlerTests.cs:32 (HandleAsync_ValidCommand_UpdatesObjectAndReturnsSuccess), :137 (HandleAsync_WithUnknownObjectId_ReturnsNotFoundAndDoesNotSave), :186 (HandleAsync_WithCustomScale_StoresScaleOnObject); AreaOutlineTests.cs:67 (SetOutline_DoesNotMoveFloorObjects); FloorObjectMethodsTests.cs:24 (AddObject_ReturnsPlacedObjectWithCorrectProperties), :41 (AddObject_SucceedsOnFloorWithNoAreas), :54 (RemoveObject_RemovesById), :79 (UpdateObject_AppliesPositionRotationAndScale), :117 (RemoveArea_LeavesObjectsInPlace); PlacedObjectTests.cs:15 (Constructor_SetsAllProperties), :45 (Update_ChangesPositionRotationAndScale), :99 (Update_InvalidScale_Throws). NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d: all 13 are scale-less there. The site list was INDEPENDENTLY RE-COUNTED by the architect in this session with its own paren-matching arity scanner (scratchpad .../architect/arity2.py, run against C:/dm-wt/6b-xiii/src), which printed 27 rows: the 4 scale-less declarations, the 1 surviving production call at FloorObjectMethods.cs:109, and exactly these 22 test sites at exactly the line numbers measurement.md section 3 lists, file for file. PREDICATE VALIDATED on that scanner: the case that must match, the live production 2-argument PlacedObject.Update call at FloorObjectMethods.cs:109, is present; the near-miss that must not, AddPlacedObjectCommandHandler.cs:24 at arity 5, is absent; the lookalike population, the local PlacedObject test helper in MapHitTesterTests.cs, is absent because the scanner requires 'new' for the constructor. The scanner's FIRST run was WRONG and is recorded here so nobody trusts it blindly: its lookbehind excluded '.', so it missed every member-access call and reported 9 rows instead of 27.

A2. THE 2 CONVERSIONS, WHICH MUST BE RENAMED. DungeonAggregateTests.AddPlacedObject_WithoutScale_ReturnsObjectWithDefaultScaleAndGivenKindPositionAndRotation (:431 at b39a65d) and DungeonAggregateTests.AddPlacedObject_WithoutScaleOnUnknownFloorId_ReturnsNull (:455 at b39a65d) BOTH SURVIVE as [Fact] test cases, each now calling the five-argument Dungeon.AddPlacedObject with ObjectScale.Default passed explicitly, and NEITHER NAME CONTAINS the substring WithoutScale, because after the conversion the name would describe something the test no longer does (test discipline, Naming: 'The name must not claim more than the test checks'). Falsifiable by two commands together: grep -c "WithoutScale" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Domain/Entities/Dungeon/DungeonAggregateTests.cs returns 0, AND grep -c "public void AddPlacedObject" on the same file returns 2. PREDICATE VALIDATED by the architect at b39a65d: grep -n "AddPlacedObject" on that file returns exactly 4 lines -- the two method names at :431 and :455 and the two calls at :439 and :462 -- so the second command counts exactly the two aggregate-level AddPlacedObject tests and nothing else, and it CANNOT be satisfied by deleting either test; and grep -n "WithoutScale" on that file returns exactly those same two name lines, so the first command cannot be satisfied by editing anything else. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d: the first command returns 2 there. THESE TWO MUST NOT BE DELETED: they are the ONLY two Dungeon.AddPlacedObject tests in DungeonAggregateTests.cs at any arity (same 4-line grep), so deleting them leaves the aggregate mutator with no aggregate-level unit test, and the unknown-floor-id-returns-null path with none at all -- AddPlacedObjectCommandHandlerTests.cs:118 covers that path at a different level and asserts ErrorCategory.NotFound, not null.

A3. THE 5 DELETED [Fact] METHODS. None of these five test methods exists anywhere under src/DungeonMaster.Tests/ any more: FloorObjectMethodsTests.UpdateObject_WithoutScaleOnExistingObject_ReturnsSuccessAndAppliesPositionAndRotation (:129 at b39a65d, subsumed by UpdateObject_AppliesPositionRotationAndScale at :76, which asserts the same Success, Position and Rotation AND additionally asserts Scale); FloorObjectMethodsTests.UpdateObject_WithoutScaleOnUnknownId_ReturnsNotFound (:152, a literal duplicate of UpdateObject_UnknownId_ReturnsNotFound at :98 once converted); PlacedObjectTests.Update_WithDefaultScale_KeepsDefaultScale (:61, whose subject is the scale-omitting call that ceases to exist); PlacedObjectTests.Update_TwoParam_PreservesCustomScale (:114, whose subject is named in its own name); ObjectKindGuardTests.FourParameterConstructor_WithNoneKind_Throws (:48, whose ObjectKind.None rejection survives at KindGuardRunsBeforeTheScaleRejection, :81). Falsifiable by: grep -rE "UpdateObject_WithoutScaleOnExistingObject|UpdateObject_WithoutScaleOnUnknownId|Update_WithDefaultScale_KeepsDefaultScale|Update_TwoParam_PreservesCustomScale|FourParameterConstructor_WithNoneKind_Throws" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/ --include=*.cs | wc -l returns 0. PREDICATE VALIDATED by the orchestrator at b39a65d, AFTER CORRECTING THE COMMAND PRE-FREEZE: with --include=*.cs it returns exactly 5, one line per name, and each of the five names is unique in the tree, so it cannot be satisfied by deleting a different test. THE --include=*.cs FILTER IS LOAD-BEARING AND MUST NOT BE DROPPED. Without it the command returns 9, not 5: xunit method names are embedded in compiled assembly metadata, so it also matches src/DungeonMaster.Tests/bin/Debug/net10.0/DungeonMaster.Tests.dll and three more copies under obj/Debug/net10.0/ (including ref/ and refint/), which grep reports as "Binary file ... matches". The architect measured 5 because it ran in the freshly created worktree C:/dm-wt/6b-xiii, which had never been built. A5 and A6 require a build and a test run in that same worktree, so by the time this criterion is reviewed those artifacts EXIST, and the uncorrected command could never return 0 no matter how correct the source edit was. It measured build output rather than source. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d.

A4. THE FOUR SURVIVORS THAT MAKE A3 SAFE. All four of these test methods still exist and still carry the assertions named, because each is the sole remaining cover for something A3 deletes: FloorObjectMethodsTests.UpdateObject_AppliesPositionRotationAndScale (asserts Success, Position, Rotation and Scale on the four-argument UpdateObject); FloorObjectMethodsTests.UpdateObject_UnknownId_ReturnsNotFound (the four-argument not-found path); ObjectKindGuardTests.KindGuardRunsBeforeTheScaleRejection (passes ObjectKind.None to the five-argument constructor and asserts ParamName == "kind" -- this is the ONLY surviving assertion that None is rejected, since FiveParameterConstructor_WithUndefinedKind_Throws passes (ObjectKind)999, not None; NOTE that A8, authorized by escalation E1 at Gate 2, ADDS an ActualValue == ObjectKind.None assertion to this same test, so A4 requires its ParamName assertion to survive and A8 requires the ActualValue one to be present -- the two are complementary, not competing, and neither licenses removing the other); PlacedObjectTests.Constructor_WithCustomScale_SetsScale (passes scale 2.0f and asserts Scale == 2.0f). THIS IS A DELIBERATE PRESERVED-BEHAVIOUR CRITERION, satisfied at b39a65d by design. It is written because A3 and A1 are otherwise satisfiable by deleting the survivors too, and because of a SIBLING-VACUITY effect A1 creates: once PlacedObjectTests.cs:15 is converted, Constructor_SetsAllProperties' assertion that Scale equals ObjectScale.Default can no longer catch a missing 'Scale = scale' assignment in the constructor, since the field initializer at PlacedObject.cs:67 supplies ObjectScale.Default on its own. Constructor_WithCustomScale_SetsScale is then the only test in the tree that can catch it.

A5. THE SOLUTION BUILDS CLEAN. Run from the worktree root, dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln --nologo prints 'Build succeeded', and its combined output piped through grep -cE "(warning|error) [A-Z]+[0-9]+" returns 0. PRESERVED-BEHAVIOUR criterion, satisfied at b39a65d (measurement.md section 7 measured the same grep at 0 there); it is written because Directory.Build.props:5 sets TreatWarningsAsErrors true, so a dangling reference or an unused local left behind by a deleted assertion is a build failure rather than a warning somebody can ignore. Use exactly this grep form: the plain form grep -icE "warning|error" ALWAYS returns at least 2 over dotnet build output, because MSBuild prints '0 Warning(s)' and '0 Error(s)' literally -- reconfirmed by the architect in this session against an unrelated scratch project whose failing build printed '0 Warning(s)' and '2 Error(s)'.

A6. DungeonMaster.Tests PASSES WITH ZERO FAILURES. dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj --nologo reports 'Failed: 0'. The passed total is PREDICTED to be 850 -- 855 at b39a65d (measurement.md section 7) minus the five [Fact] deletions in A3, with the two A2 conversions keeping their cases. THAT FIGURE IS A PREDICTION, NOT A MEASUREMENT: the verdict on this criterion turns on 'Failed: 0' alone, and any total other than 850 must be reconciled against A3 and A2 and REPORTED as a surprise, never rationalised into agreement. DungeonMaster.Tests is the only assembly this task can affect: the five members are internal to DungeonMaster.Domain and the only InternalsVisibleTo grant it issues is to DungeonMaster.Tests (src/DungeonMaster.Domain/AssemblyInfo.cs:3, the sole line in that file), so no App-side assembly can reference them at all -- verified by the ORCHESTRATOR at b39a65d, correcting the architect's count pre-freeze: grep -rn "InternalsVisibleTo" over src/ --include=*.cs --include=*.csproj --include=*.props (excluding bin/ and obj/) returns 8 lines, of which exactly 5 are real [assembly: InternalsVisibleTo(...)] attributes -- DungeonMaster.App to App.Tests, App.Core to Tests, Application to Tests, Domain to Tests, and Tests to DynamicProxyGenAssembly2 -- and the other 3 are the string appearing inside XML doc comments. The architect reported 6 attribute lines; there are 5. The load-bearing half is unaffected and was re-verified: src/DungeonMaster.Domain/AssemblyInfo.cs:3 is the ONLY grant Domain issues and it names DungeonMaster.Tests alone, so no App-side assembly can reference the five members at all. Counted with grep -rn "^\[assembly: InternalsVisibleTo" src/ --include=*.cs, which returns 5. The solution-wide suite is checked by T2's B10 once the deletion has landed.

A7. THE COMMAND-LEVEL DEFAULT IS NOT COLLATERAL DAMAGE. UpdatePlacedObjectCommandHandlerTests.HandleAsync_ValidCommand_UpdatesObjectAndReturnsSuccess still asserts that obj.Scale is approximately ObjectScale.Default after HandleAsync, and the UpdatePlacedObjectCommand it constructs still OMITS the NewScale argument. PRESERVED-BEHAVIOUR criterion, satisfied at b39a65d by design. It is written because measurement.md section 5.4 flags this test for a second look on the grounds that its body touches scale, and the second look resolves in favour of leaving the assertion alone: the assertion is about the COMMAND's default, which comes from 'float NewScale = ObjectScale.Default' at src/DungeonMaster.Application/Features/Dungeons/Commands/UpdatePlacedObject/UpdatePlacedObjectCommand.cs:34 (read by the architect at b39a65d), and is entirely independent of the deleted aggregate overload. The scale-less call in this test is arrange-only setup and A1 covers appending to it. Deleting the :61 assertion as part of this session would remove live coverage of a default this session does not touch.

A8. THE ObjectKind.None ActualValue ASSERTION IS PRESERVED, AND IT MOVES BEFORE THE DELETION REMOVES IT. ObjectKindGuardTests.KindGuardRunsBeforeTheScaleRejection asserts BOTH that the thrown ArgumentOutOfRangeException's ParamName is "kind" AND that its ActualValue is ObjectKind.None. AUTHORIZED BY ESCALATION E1, resolved by the user at Gate 2 BEFORE the freeze, which is why this is an ordinary criterion and not an amendment: the approved scope covers the 22 call sites and this test is not one of them, so permission to touch it was the user's to give. WHY IT EXISTS: A3 deletes FourParameterConstructor_WithNoneKind_Throws, which at b39a65d is the ONLY test in the tree asserting that the ActualValue for the ObjectKind.None case IS None (ObjectKindGuardTests.cs:59-60). FiveParameterConstructor_WithUndefinedKind_Throws asserts ActualValue == (ObjectKind)999, not None (:77), and KindGuardRunsBeforeTheScaleRejection asserts ParamName only (:90-91). Without this criterion A3 silently drops that coverage. FALSIFIABLE BY, and the form matters: awk '/public void KindGuardRunsBeforeTheScaleRejection/,/^\t}$/' src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Domain/Entities/Floor/ObjectKindGuardTests.cs | grep -c "ActualValue.Should().Be(ObjectKind.None)" returns 1. A FLAT COUNT OVER THE FILE CANNOT CHECK THIS AND MUST NOT BE SUBSTITUTED -- the orchestrator measured it: grep -c "ActualValue.Should().Be(ObjectKind.None)" over the whole file returns 1 at b39a65d and would still return 1 after the change, because the assertion is not being added to the tree, it is being MOVED from the deleted test into the surviving one. The flat form is vacuous by construction. PREDICATE VALIDATED WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL by the orchestrator at b39a65d: the awk-scoped command returns 0 against KindGuardRunsBeforeTheScaleRejection, which is the case that must not match yet, and the identical form aimed at FourParameterConstructor_WithNoneKind_Throws returns 1, which is the control that must match -- so the command is reading the method body it names rather than the file. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d. ORDERING: make this edit BEFORE deleting the four-parameter test, so that no state of the working tree has the assertion in neither place.

tasks.title: Delete the five scale-less Domain overloads named in measurement.md section 3 (MASTER-047 / CORE-019)
acceptance: B1. Dungeon.AddPlacedObject(Guid, ObjectKind, CanvasPoint, ObjectRotation) -- the four-parameter overload at src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Dungeons/DungeonMethods.cs:371-381 at b39a65d, whose whole body is a delegation to the five-parameter overload with ObjectScale.Default -- no longer exists, and neither does its XML doc comment block immediately above it. After the edit, Dungeon declares AddPlacedObject exactly once and that declaration takes five parameters. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d. Note for the reader: :371 is the CORRECTED location. CORE-019 cites :323-333 for this member, which is stale -- :323-333 is UpdateAreaOutline (measurement.md section 2). [AMENDED by escalation E2, 2026-09-29: this range was corrected from :371-377 to :371-381. :371-377 was authored by the orchestrator at Gate 1 by inferring the span's end from two grep hits instead of reading it, and it cuts off mid-expression after '=> AddPlacedObject(' and 'floorId,'. The member's signature is :371-375 and its delegating body :376-381; its doc comment is :353-370. Caught by T2's implementer, which measured the range before deleting it.]

B2. Floor.AddObject(ObjectKind, CanvasPoint, ObjectRotation) -- the three-parameter overload at src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/FloorObjectMethods.cs:7-14 at b39a65d (doc comment at :7-9, signature at :10-13, delegating body at :14) -- no longer exists, doc comment included. After the edit, Floor declares AddObject exactly once and that declaration takes four parameters. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d.

B3. Floor.UpdateObject(Guid, CanvasPoint, ObjectRotation) -- the three-parameter overload at src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/FloorObjectMethods.cs:79-113 at b39a65d -- no longer exists, doc comment included. After the edit, Floor declares UpdateObject exactly once and that declaration takes four parameters. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d. This deletion also removes the ONLY surviving production call to the two-parameter PlacedObject.Update, which sits inside this method's body at FloorObjectMethods.cs:109, and that is what makes B5 possible: B3 must land in the same change as B5, or B5 leaves a dangling call.

B4. The four-parameter internal PlacedObject(Guid, ObjectKind, CanvasPoint, ObjectRotation) constructor -- at src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/PlacedObject.cs:12-18 at b39a65d (doc comment at :12, signature at :13-17, ': this(...)' delegation at :18) -- no longer exists, doc comment included. After the edit, PlacedObject declares exactly two constructors: the private parameterless one and the five-parameter internal one. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d.

B5. PlacedObject.Update(CanvasPoint, ObjectRotation) -- the two-parameter overload at src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/PlacedObject.cs:69-71 at b39a65d (doc comment at :69, signature at :70, delegating body at :71) -- no longer exists, doc comment included. After the edit, PlacedObject declares Update exactly once and that declaration takes three parameters. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d. Note for the reader: :69-71 is the CORRECTED location. CORE-019 cites :62-63 for this member, which is stale -- :62-63 is the Rotation property's doc comment (measurement.md section 2).

B6. The Scale property's field initializer in src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/PlacedObject.cs -- 'public float Scale { get; private set; } = ObjectScale.Default;' at :67 at b39a65d -- is unchanged, initializer included. PRESERVED-BEHAVIOUR criterion, satisfied at b39a65d by design. It is written because the initializer LOOKS like a sixth member of the dead cluster and is not: the private parameterless constructor at :10 is EF Core's materialization path and assigns nothing, so this initializer is the only thing that sets Scale on that path (measurement.md section 6). Removing it would silently give every entity materialized from the database a scale of 0, which is below ObjectScale.Min and which no test in the suite would necessarily catch.

B7. The private parameterless constructor 'private PlacedObject() { }' at src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/PlacedObject.cs:10 at b39a65d is unchanged. PRESERVED-BEHAVIOUR criterion, satisfied at b39a65d by design, and written for the same reason as B6: it is EF Core's materialization path, it takes no arguments, and a reader deleting 'the constructor that takes no scale' could reach for it.

B8. src/DungeonMaster.Domain/AssemblyInfo.cs is unchanged -- it still consists of the single '[assembly: InternalsVisibleTo("DungeonMaster.Tests")]' attribute and its using directive, 3 lines total (counted by the architect with cat -n at b39a65d). PRESERVED-BEHAVIOUR criterion, satisfied at b39a65d by design. It is written because CORE-019 lists AssemblyInfo.cs:3 as the sixth of its six locations, so an implementer working from the entry rather than from this manifest could read the grant as part of what the entry directs removing. It is not: it is the grant the REST of DungeonMaster.Tests reaches Domain internals through. The file is also outside this task's ownership set, so touching it is an ownership violation as well as a criterion failure.

B9. THE SOLUTION BUILDS CLEAN, WHICH IS ALSO THE PROOF THAT T1 WAS COMPLETE. Run from the worktree root, dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln --nologo prints 'Build succeeded', and its combined output piped through grep -cE "(warning|error) [A-Z]+[0-9]+" returns 0. PRESERVED-BEHAVIOUR criterion in form -- the solution also builds clean at b39a65d -- but its CONTENT changes once B1 through B5 have landed, and that is the point of writing it here rather than only on T1: with the five overloads gone, any scale-less call site T1 missed is a COMPILE ERROR, not a warning somebody can suppress. MEASURED CLAIM, not assumed: the architect built a scratch project in this session in which a three-parameter method and a three-parameter constructor were each called with two arguments, and the compiler emitted 'error CS7036: There is no argument given that corresponds to the required parameter' for BOTH, at error severity, with '0 Warning(s)' and '2 Error(s)' in the summary. The diagnostic is CS7036 in both the method and the constructor case -- NOT CS1501, which is what an unverified guess would have written here. Use exactly the grep form given: the plain form grep -icE "warning|error" always returns at least 2 over dotnet build output because MSBuild prints '0 Warning(s)' and '0 Error(s)' literally.

B10. THE WHOLE SUITE PASSES WITH ZERO FAILURES. dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.sln --nologo reports 'Failed: 0' for all three test assemblies. Read each assembly's identity from its 'Test run for ...' line, NOT from the 'Passed!' lines: the 'Passed!' line prints '(net10.0)' for all three including DungeonMaster.App.Tests, which demonstrably runs from bin/Debug/net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0, so the 'Passed!' line cannot tell you which framework ran (measurement.md section 7, where this reproduced). Predicted totals: DungeonMaster.Tests 850, DungeonMaster.App.UnitTests 23, DungeonMaster.App.Tests 102, total 975, against 855 / 23 / 102 / 980 at b39a65d. THOSE ARE PREDICTIONS, NOT MEASUREMENTS: the verdict turns on 'Failed: 0', and any other total must be reported as a surprise to investigate rather than reconciled by assertion. A criterion phrased 'the suite count is unchanged' would be unsatisfiable here by construction and must not be substituted. PRESERVED-BEHAVIOUR on the zero-failures clause. If DungeonMaster.App is running, this command fails with MSB3026 or MSB3027 on a locked file rather than on any test: close the app first, and do not read a file-lock failure as a test failure.

B11. NOTHING OUTSIDE THE FIVE MEMBERS IS DELETED FROM THE THREE OWNED FILES. Each of the three files still declares every other member it declared at b39a65d: DungeonMethods.cs still declares the five-parameter AddPlacedObject and the single UpdatePlacedObject (which has exactly one declaration and requires newScale -- measurement.md section 4.2); FloorObjectMethods.cs still declares the four-parameter AddObject, RemoveObject and the four-parameter UpdateObject; PlacedObject.cs still declares FloorId, Kind, Position, Rotation, Scale and the three-parameter Update with its full scale guard. PRESERVED-BEHAVIOUR criterion, satisfied at b39a65d by design. It is written because the five deletions are interleaved with their live twins in all three files -- doc comment, dead overload, doc comment, live overload -- so an over-wide deletion is the most likely way this task goes wrong, and B9 alone would not catch the removal of a member nothing in the suite calls.

tasks.title: Repair CORE-019's two stale citations, amend the entry, and write MASTER-047's closure into the master index without a commit hash (measurement.md section 2)
acceptance: C1. CORE-019's locations list no longer carries the first stale citation. Falsifiable by: grep -c "src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Dungeons/DungeonMethods.cs:323-333" docs/audit/01-domain-application.md returns 0. PREDICATE VALIDATED by the architect at b39a65d, and THE SHORT FORM OF THIS COMMAND IS A TRAP THAT MUST NOT BE USED: grep -rn "DungeonMethods.cs:323-333" docs/ returns TWO lines, :933 which is CORE-019's, and :211 which belongs to CORE-004 and cites 'Entities/Dungeon/DungeonMethods.cs:323-333' with the pre-pluralisation singular folder name. CORE-004 is a naming entry ABOUT those namespaces and its old paths are its own historical subject; it is out of scope and must not be edited. The full-path form with 'Dungeons/' returns exactly 1 -- the case that must match is :933, the near-miss that must not is :211, and the full path separates them. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d: the full-path command returns 1 there.

C2. CORE-019's locations list names the scale-less Dungeon.AddPlacedObject at src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Dungeons/DungeonMethods.cs:371-381, and that entry is qualified in the record as the member's position AT b39a65d rather than as a current line range. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d: grep -rc "DungeonMethods.cs:371-381" over docs/ returns 0 in every file there, counted by the architect at b39a65d. The qualification is required because T2 deletes those lines, so an unqualified range sends a later reader to code that no longer exists and reads as a second drift defect. [AMENDED by escalation E2, 2026-09-29: this range was corrected from :371-377 to :371-381. :371-377 was authored by the orchestrator at Gate 1 by inferring the span's end from two grep hits instead of reading it, and it cuts off mid-expression after '=> AddPlacedObject(' and 'floorId,'. The member's signature is :371-375 and its delegating body :376-381; its doc comment is :353-370. Caught by T2's implementer, which measured the range before deleting it.]

C3. CORE-019's locations list no longer carries the second stale citation. Falsifiable by: grep -c "src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/PlacedObject.cs:62-63" docs/audit/01-domain-application.md returns 0. PREDICATE VALIDATED by the architect at b39a65d: this string matches exactly one line in the whole of docs/, :937, which is CORE-019's fifth locations entry, so unlike C1 there is no near-miss to separate -- but use the full-path form anyway, for symmetry with C1 and because the bare filename is not unique in the tree. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d: the command returns 1 there.

C4. CORE-019's locations list names the two-parameter PlacedObject.Update at src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/PlacedObject.cs:69-71, qualified as its position AT b39a65d. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d: grep -rc "PlacedObject.cs:69-71" over docs/ returns 0 in every file there, counted by the architect at b39a65d.

C5. An AMENDED block for this sub-session exists in CORE-019's body, in the form the register already uses (see docs/audit/04-app-controls-and-theme.md:408 for a citation-repair amendment and docs/audit/01-domain-application.md:299 for 6b-xii's), opening with 'AMENDED 6b-xiii, 2026-09-29' and carrying a 'Classification:' verdict of DRIFT. It quotes BOTH corrected citations' previous wording verbatim -- 'src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Dungeons/DungeonMethods.cs:323-333' and 'src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/PlacedObject.cs:62-63' -- and states what each of those ranges actually holds: UpdateAreaOutline, and the Rotation property's doc comment. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d: no AMENDED block exists in CORE-019.

C6. That amendment states the CAUSE and the direction of the drift: neither stale citation was caused by any work on MASTER-047, and both were caused by the ObjectScale feature work inserting the scale-carrying overloads above and beside the scale-less ones -- the same mechanism 6b-xii recorded when CORE-006's fix falsified CORE-005, namely that a fix aimed at one entry silently falsifies its neighbours in prose, at lines that may never move. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d.

C7. That amendment states that the two corrected ranges, and the entry's in-prose citation of FloorObjectMethods.cs:109 -- which was CORRECT at b39a65d, the one in-prose citation the measurement checked and found sound -- are historical positions at b39a65d and are NOT navigable at HEAD, because all three point at code this session deleted. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d, where all three ranges are live and the qualification would be false.

C8. MASTER-047's Status cell in docs/audit/00-master-index.md -- the last cell of the table row whose second column is MASTER-047, at :235 at b39a65d -- is non-empty and begins '**done** (6b-xiii)', AND CONTAINS NO COMMIT HASH. The hash is deliberately absent: a DIR task cannot invoke git, and this register's own convention, stated explicitly in the MASTER-098 and MASTER-163 amendments in this same file, is that a closure's commit evidence is written by the orchestrator at Gate 3 and must not be guessed by the task. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d: the architect read line 235 with awk and split it on '|' -- 12 fields, of which the last content field is a single space. Note that the no-hash half of this criterion is trivially true of that empty cell, so it is written as one criterion with the '**done** (6b-xiii)' half rather than as two; only jointly does it exclude the current state.

C9. That Status cell records the three-way disposition of the tests, because a later reader cannot recover it from CORE-019, whose suggested direction says only 'update the tests to pass ObjectScale.Default explicitly' and anticipates no deletions: 5 xunit [Fact] cases DELETED by name, 2 CONVERTED AND RENAMED by name, and 13 sites mechanically appended. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d.

C10. That Status cell records that 2 of CORE-019's 6 locations were stale when re-measured at b39a65d, names which 2, and points the reader at the amendment in docs/audit/01-domain-application.md rather than restating it. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d.

C11. That Status cell records the suite total measured AFTER the change alongside the 980 measured at b39a65d, taking the after figure from T2's own measured B10 output as handed to this task by the orchestrator at dispatch, and NOT from measurement.md section 5.5, whose 975 is explicitly a prediction. If the two disagree the cell says so and says which is the measurement. NOT SATISFIED AT b39a65d.
